newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Novartis aims to be leader in generic drugs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Novartis aims to be leader in generic drugs.

text.p: The designated boss of Novartis Inc said on Tuesday he was determined to make the Swiss phamaceuticals company arising from the merger of Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG the world leader in fast-growing generic drugs.

Sandoz's purchase of Azupharma GmbH, Germany's third-largest generic drugs company, for 640 million marks ($416 million) from Germany's Gehe AG underscored this strategy, Daniel Vasella told Reuters after the deal was announced.

"Buying a company which has an important position as number three in Germany, which is the second-largest generics market in the world, puts us in a position where we will be becoming the number one company in generics worldwide," he said.
Both Sandoz and Ciba-Geigy already had significant businesses in generics, drugs that are not protected by patents and thus face fierce competition.
Sandoz specialises in bulk manufacturing, especially of antibiotics, while Ciba-Geigy's focus was on retail generics.
Combined with Azupharm, the companies' total generics turnover would amount to some 1.4 billion Swiss francs ($1.11 billion) a year, a company spokesman said.

Vasella noted that this was small change compared with volumes in branded patented drugs, but added worldwide demand for generic pharmaceuticals was growing rapidly at a rate of nearly 11 percent a year.
"I don't see any reason why increases in generics' growth should slow down significantly," he said.

"It is an industry which, under the auspices of health care cost containment, which is a worldwide phenomenon, will continue to play a very important role. It is in itself growing faster than the branded pharmaceutical market."
A bigger generics operation will also let Novartis offer large customers a broader product line and give it an edge in launching generics based on its own products as patents expire.

"You can extend the life of the product and the cash flow by introducing your own generic. As owner of the product, you also have the opportunity to launch it just before the competition, which means being first on the market. And being first is key because the first one gets the lion's share of the market."
He said Azupharma was attractive in part because Gehe was getting out of the drugs manufacturing business and was looking to sell its operations in that field.
"Of course it's an opportunuity, but an opportunity which fits our strategic intent to be an important player in all the businesses we are competing in," Vasella said.
Based in Gerlingen near Stuttgart, Azupharma employs 440 people and generated sales of 222 million marks in 1995. Branded generics account for 80 percent of sales.
Vasella said he was not actively seeking other acquisition targets in the field.

"There is neither an urgency nor a specific need, but I would say if a piece would be available that would fit our intention, that is fine. But our first objective is internal growth," he said by telephone by Basle.
Vasella said he was confident margins on generic products could be kept "significantly" above the five or six percent common in the United States, but he did not elaborate.

Generics will always play a subordinate role for Novartis's paharmaceutical division, Vasella made clear. "It is not an alternative to the research- and innovation-led part of the business. It is a complement and not a replacement," he said.
($1=1.2646 Swiss Franc)
